column2: On the authority of Abū Ḥamzah Anas ibn Mālik (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him), the servant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.” Reported by al-Bukhārī and Muslim.
This hadith negates the completeness of obligatory faith in a Muslim until he loves for his Muslim brother what he loves for himself, in matters of this world and the Hereafter.

Included in this is that he treats people as he would like them to treat him. It has come in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim (1844) from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ (may Allah be pleased with them both), in a long hadith:

“Whoever would love to be moved away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise, let his death come to him while he believes in Allah and the Last Day, and let him treat people the way he would love to be treated.”

And Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: “Woe to those who give short measure, who, when they take a measure from people, take in full, but when they measure or weigh for them, give less” [al-Muṭaffifīn 83:1–3].

The ḥāfiẓ Ibn Rajab said in Jāmiʿ al-ʿUlūm wa-l-Ḥikam (1/306): “The hadith of Anas shows that the believer is pleased by what pleases his believing brother, and wants for his believing brother the good that he wants for himself.
All of this comes only from a heart completely free of rancour, deceit and envy; for envy requires the envier to dislike anyone surpassing him in some good, or equalling him in it,

because he loves to be distinguished above people by his virtues and to have them to himself; faith requires the opposite of that, namely that all the believers share with him the good that Allah has given him, without any of it being diminished for him.”

He also said (1/308): “In sum, the believer should love for the believers what he loves for himself, and dislike for them what he dislikes for himself. If he sees some deficiency in his Muslim brother's religion, he strives to set it right.”
A Muslim should love for his Muslim brother what he loves for himself, and dislike for him what he dislikes for himself.
since the completeness of obligatory faith is negated from him until he is like this.
The believers differ in degree in their faith.
Using the expression “his brother” is meant to soften the Muslim's heart so that he does this for his brother.
